correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md proof and independently derived equilibrium x2=(1+a lambda)/(2+b lambda), x1=(1+(b-a)lambda)/(2+b lambda) on the positive-flow interval. When b<a, x1 reaches 0 at lambda*=1/(a-b), and unused-route inequality lambda a>=1+lambda b makes x2=1 valid thereafter. Unique equilibrium follows strict increases of both perceived costs. Symbolic differentiation gives G prime=(2a-b)(2b x2-a)/(2+b lambda)^2, with x2 prime=(2a-b)/(2+b lambda)^2. For b<a, x2 goes from 1/2 to 1 and the sign factor crosses 0 exactly if a/2<b<a; for b>=a, x2 prime changes sign at b=2a, while 2b x2-a>0 for b>=a. All equality endpoints checked; for a=b=1, G=(lambda^2+3lambda+3)/(lambda+2)^2 and G prime=lambda/(lambda+2)^3>0 for lambda>0. Independent sympy derivative equality and seven boundary/representative parameter checks corroborate; analytic sign proof covers all positive ratios.

value.rationale: A motivated minimal-network sharp boundary for the failure of a published constant-externality monotonicity principle, with a full five-regime classification rather than a single illustrative counterexample. The two-route construction removes Braess topology and can inform exact test cases in traffic-pricing theory. Its algebra is elementary, but the natural minimality and sharp coefficient thresholds carry the specific scientific value; no claim to general traffic models.

final_claim: For Wardrop equilibrium with unit demand on two parallel routes having travel times x1,x2, priced per-unit externalities a and b*x2 (a,b>0), aggregate G=a*x1+b*x2^2 decreases then stabilizes if b<=a/2, decreases then increases before stabilizing if a/2<b<a, strictly increases if a<=b<2a, is constant if b=2a, and strictly decreases if b>2a, with saturation lambda*=1/(a-b) when b<a.
limitations: Only fixed unit demand, two parallel links with equal unit-slope travel time and g1=a,g2=b*x2.
Flow-dependent emission proxy is not an empirical emissions claim.
Priority could be an unindexed Wardrop classroom example; not an unconditional new-model theorem.
